decision: D115 §一.4 and §三 — the JavaScript the Web framework ships, both as a velar/* module and as the runtime it inlines into an emitted program, is real source that the JavaScript parser checks, not a template literal nothing can lint.

constants.name: WEB_DOM_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: /** The captured DOM ABI both `velar/web` and an emitted program's own JSX reach the document through. */

constants.name: WEB_REACTIVITY_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: /** The captured Object/Array/Set/Map ABI the dependency graph is built out of. */

constants.name: WEB_ERROR_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: /** Error normalization plus the Web-owned promise and freeze operations layered on it. */

constants.name: WEB_RUNTIME_FOUNDATION
documentation: * The reactive runtime an application installs once: the captured host ABI,
* the flush budget and its runaway report, and the dependency graph itself.
* `velar/app` ships it as a module; an emitted program inlines the same
* bytes, because both are this constant.

constants.name: WEB_RUNTIME_FOUNDATION_SHARED_ERROR
documentation: * The same foundation for a project build, where error normalization is
* imported from the compiler-owned module instead of inlined.

constants.name: CSS_STRING_RUNTIME_BODY
documentation: * `cssString` written as emitted-runtime JavaScript. The runtime spelling and
* the compile-time spelling must produce the same text for the same input —
* a Look string folded at compile time and the same string pushed through the
* runtime are the same declaration — so they are published together.

constants.name: VELAR_REACTIVE_BRIDGE_RUNTIME
documentation: /** Web-owned late-binding bridge to its optional immutable reactive runtime provider. */

constants.name: VELAR_REACTIVE_COLLECTION_BRIDGE_RUNTIME
documentation: /** Collection-only extension of the Web reactive bridge. */

constants.name: VELAR_REACTIVE_BRIDGE_MODULE_SOURCE
documentation: /** The shared reactive-bridge module a project build imports, bridge plus collections plus its export block. */

constants.name: VELAR_WEB_REALTIME_CLIENT_RUNTIME
documentation: /** Browser-owned resilient realtime client layered over `velar/websocket`. */

constants.name: WEB_BROWSER_REQUIRE_HOST_RUNTIME
documentation: * The one refusal `velar/browser` gives when there is no browser under it.
* D114 0.29.0 LC-I1: "there is no browser here" is one fact, and it used to
* arrive in four sentences — two of them field validations ("Browser online
* state must be bool") that sent the author to check his own data, and two
* spellings of "The browser does not expose native …" that differed by a word.
* `velar/storage` already answers this in one sentence at the call that needed
* the host, and the charter's standard-library membership boundary requires the
* failure to arrive there rather than at the import; this is that sentence for
* `velar/browser`.
* The document is the host's own evidence: every guarded entry reads `window`,
* `navigator`, `location` or the document itself, and none of the four exists
* without it. With a document present, every entry behaves exactly as it did —
* an argument is still checked before the host is touched, and a clipboard
* outside a secure context still says so.

constants.name: WEB_FILE_TYPE_RUNTIME
documentation: /** `is File` for a value the compiler could not prove, read through the registry's own descriptor. */

constants.name: LOOK_ARITHMETIC_RUNTIME
documentation: /** Look unit arithmetic, for the modules whose `look:` values the compiler could not fold. */

constants.name: WEB_RUNTIME_BODY
documentation: * The Web runtime an emitted program carries inside itself: reporting,
* observers and cells, managed async, component scopes, the DOM writer, and
* the look/class/style appliers. `webRuntime` splices the module's own
* keyword table into it; everything else here is the same for every program.

assemblies.name: velar web emitted runtime (shared error normalization)
